summary:
The memory work has two parts, and both are prototypes. Nothing in this area is ready to push upstream.

(1) The Hermes lane for z0evals#56 is branch study/hermes-unified-memory-56. It is local only, at c84663880a, two commits on fork main 5000e29936, and has not been pushed to the fork. It adds evals/unified_memory/{bridge,run,study}.py, a copy of agent/memory_packet_cache.py that no core code imports, and tests. It changes no core Hermes module. It drives the unmodified z0int pre_llm_call adapter (an ordinary hook plugin, not a MemoryProvider). That adapter's `invoke` is rebound to PacketBridge, which calls z0int.resolve_context, adds content SHA-256 versions on every lookup, refuses to cache gaps, and keeps a process-local delivery ledger. Injection lands in the per-turn user sidecar and is proven through pre_api_request captures. A live smoke run on Nous/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 produced 4 receipts (cold, warm, source-revision, missing-evidence), all verified and valid against the PR57 schema. 62 deterministic tests passed and 2 mutation guards failed as intended.

The frozen gate passed nothing: blocker.json shows exit 2 and model_called=false, because the cohort was not frozen at delivery time. A cohort has been frozen since then, but it does not unblock the lane. PR59's cohort.json is an OMP-promoted synthetic fixture. The source-slot cohort (executable-cohort.v1, on the unmerged z0evals branch study/executable-unified-memory-56 at 667223e) uses a different answer contract (status/facts/provenance/superseded/missing_slots) and AgentsView message sources. Its READINESS says preflight passed=false: the conflict_a/b slots are unbound, 0 prompts are instantiated and there are 0 receipts. The Hermes lane would need a v1 adapter and the contradiction sources before it can run the cohort.

(2) Fork branch memory-packet-cache (3e762e9d8f) adds a last-known-good recall cache inside MemoryManager._prefetch_provider, with 30 tests. Reading the code turned up three blockers:
- run_agent._sync_external_memory_for_turn calls sync_all after every completed turn, and that call invalidates the cache. So a "fresh" hit cannot happen across completed turns. The only fresh case left is an interrupted turn retried with the same query within 30 s.
- After a write, the stale (pre-write) packet is injected unmarked for up to 300 s. A test on that branch asserts this behaviour.
- start_refresh starts a bare threading.Thread, which breaks the spawn_context_thread rule for profile and secret scope.

The speed evidence is synthetic: 0.09 ms vs 1.03 ms against a fake provider. It also clashes with upstream's MemoryProvider.prefetch contract, which makes providers responsible for caching. Four of the seven in-tree providers already queue_prefetch, and mem0 caches per query. The backend that motivated it, memory_tencentdb, is an out-of-tree plugin, so that plugin is the natural home for the cache under policy.

Promotable now: nothing upstream. The upstream-fit candidates are prefetch outcome telemetry (it extends teknium's 25c1b008c8 telemetry wiring) and a deterministic evals/memory prefetch fault probe, following the evals/memory/honcho_current_query.py precedent. The other items stay research or downstream. The "62 tests passed" figure comes from the lane's saved logs; tests were not run in this read-only phase.
architecture_notes:
Hermes memory architecture, read at upstream main 663362680b (wt0); h.git main is 298a01c79b.
- MemoryManager (agent/memory_manager.py) holds the builtin store plus at most one external provider (add_provider rejects a second).
- prefetch_all strips skill scaffolding, then calls _prefetch_provider for each provider. An external provider runs on a spawn_context_thread with an in-flight guard: if the previous call is still running, it returns "" and skips that turn. _EXTERNAL_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S is 8.0. Results are spilled when oversized (spill_if_oversized).
- Prefetch runs synchronously on the turn critical path: agent/turn_context.py build -> _memory_turn_start_and_prefetch, which skips trivial prompts via is_trivial_prompt. The result is stamped into the current user turn's api_content sidecar (_stamp_api_content_sidecar) and replayed verbatim on later turns. It never goes into the system prompt.
- pre_llm_call plugin context goes through _collect_pre_llm_call_context (line 754). That function passes session_id/task_id/turn_id/user_message/etc. to hooks, spills oversized context, and merges it into the same user-message sidecar.
- run_agent._sync_external_memory_for_turn (run_agent.py:919-950) calls sync_all and then queue_prefetch_all after every completed, non-interrupted turn.

Contracts:
- The MemoryProvider ABC (agent/memory_provider.py) says prefetch "Must be fast — recall in the background and return cached results". Caching is the provider's job.
- spawn_context_thread docstring: "Every memory-provider background job (prefetch, sync, writer loops) must go through this". This preserves the ContextVar HERMES_HOME override and the per-turn secret scope.
- VALID_HOOKS (hermes_cli/plugins.py:107) includes pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, post_api_request and pre/post_auxiliary_call. These are the policy-endorsed extension surface.

Policy (CONTRIBUTING.md:70-84):
- The set of built-in memory providers (honcho, mem0, supermemory, byterover, holographic, openviking, retaindb) is closed. New backends ship as standalone plugins, using the same ABC and discover_memory_providers.
- Third-party integrations, z0int included, ship as standalone plugins that use generic hooks. A capability the framework lacks should become a request to widen the generic plugin surface.
- The unified-memory lane follows this: z0int is a pre_llm_call hook plugin and Hermes core is untouched.
- Telemetry: 25c1b008c8 (2026-09-27) records memory tool calls via shared_metrics_loop.record_provider_memory_call. Prefetch is not instrumented.
- Upstream evals/memory/honcho_current_query.py sets a precedent: deterministic local-fixture probes with no hosted service and no inference are acceptable upstream.

Seams the lane depends on:
- PluginContext.register_hook
- _collect_pre_llm_call_context (private function; a coupling risk)
- AIAgent(skip_memory, skip_context_files, skip_background_review, enabled_toolsets=[], max_iterations=2)
- load_config_readonly and resolve_runtime_provider

Operational notes:
- Running a linked worktree whose .git lives inside the live Hermes home trips the home-I/O guard. Verification therefore used a separate checkout, /workspace/zer0/worktrees/hermes-memory-56-verification at the same SHA.
- Upstream moves fast: 451 commits between 5000e29936 and main, and 6913 since the cache base afc3b7c6f3. Upstream's memory_manager.py changes since afc3b7c6f3 don't overlap the cache patch's hunks, so a clean rebase is likely but unverified.

features.title: Hermes lane for z0evals#56 source-backed memory study (z0int pre_llm_call adapter + PacketBridge eval harness)
features.description: An opt-in eval harness with this pipeline: explicit source pointers -> real z0int.resolve_context EvidenceRefs -> MemoryPacketCache (scoped, content-SHA keyed) -> unmodified z0int Hermes adapter register/before_turn, with invoke rebound to PacketBridge (the z0int automatic router is bypassed) -> real pre_llm_call -> per-turn user sidecar -> pre_api_request capture -> a live AIAgent call -> an exact structured verifier {answer,citations,abstained} -> PR57 receipt JSONL. A frozen-input gate refuses the family-label scaffold, and --smoke is labelled as not the frozen cohort.
features.hermes_integration_point: New files only: evals/unified_memory/{bridge.py,run.py,study.py,README.md,receipt.schema.json,question-contract.json,smoke-manifest.schema.json}, tests/evals/{test_unified_memory.py,conftest.py}, plus an unused copy of agent/memory_packet_cache.py. It consumes hermes_cli.plugins.PluginContext.register_hook('pre_llm_call'|'pre_api_request'|'post_api_request'), agent.turn_context._collect_pre_llm_call_context (private), run_agent.AIAgent, hermes_cli.config.load_config_readonly and hermes_cli.runtime_provider.resolve_runtime_provider. Core Hermes behavior is unchanged.

evidence.finding: 5 integration tests plus 57 regression tests (21 cache, 28 api_content_sidecar, 2 detached-fork lifecycle, 6 memory hook registration) passed at c84663880a, exit 0

Removing the replay guard made the test fail with duplicate context. Removing the content-SHA revision check made a same-size, same-mtime source replacement serve stale 'alpha'. So mtime:size freshness alone is unsafe.

Live smoke on nous/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: 4/4 receipts verified and schema-valid (cold, warm, source-revision, missing-evidence). Injected exactly once per request, no duplicate injection, replay suppressed 4/4, abstained correctly when the source was removed. n=1 per arm.
Frozen gate blocked: 'Missing or invalid frozen DSH prompts, source pointers, or verification oracle'. Exit 2, model_called=false. Nothing passed the frozen gate.

The cohort frozen after delivery uses a different answer contract (status/facts/provenance/superseded/missing_slots) and AgentsView message bindings. Preflight passed=false: conflict_a/b unbound, 4/6 slots bound, 0 instantiated prompts, 0 receipts. The lane's verifier and exact_path transport do not match it.

features.policy_notes: Adds no memory provider and changes no core code. z0int is consumed as a generic pre_llm_call hook plugin, which is the path CONTRIBUTING endorses. The harness depends on a pinned external z0int checkout (c4a4554) and on z0evals schemas, so it belongs in z0evals/z0int or the fork's lab/, not in NousResearch upstream. The copied agent/memory_packet_cache.py would be dead core code in any upstream PR.
features.risks: The answer contract and source model don't match executable-cohort.v1, so the lane needs an adapter that calls z0evals cohort_contract.preflight/verify_answer. It couples to the private _collect_pre_llm_call_context. The replay ledger is process-local and bounded to 1024 entries. The branch is unpushed and exists only on local disk. The cohort itself is blocked on genuine contradiction sources. Latency figures are n=1.

features.title: Scoped, policy-versioned last-known-good recall cache in MemoryManager._prefetch_provider
features.description: MemoryPacketCache has a 30 s fresh window and a 300 s stale window, keeps at most 512 entries, never caches empty text, and puts POLICY_VERSION in every key. An optional provider cache_scope() can widen scope across sessions. sync_all marks scope packets stale instead of deleting them. A stale hit is served immediately while a coalesced background refresh runs.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/memory_packet_cache.py (new). agent/memory_manager.py: __init__, _packet_scope, invalidate_memory_packets (called from sync_all), _spill_packet, _refresh_packet, _fetch_provider_bounded, _prefetch_provider. Optional MemoryProvider.cache_scope(). Invalidation is triggered every turn by run_agent.py:_sync_external_memory_for_turn.

evidence.finding: 30 tests: 21 cache-unit and 9 manager-level. test_stale_packet_is_injected_now_... asserts that the pre-write 'v1 memory' is injected after invalidation. No test covers profile or contextvar propagation.

Against a fake provider, warm took 0.09 ms vs 1.03 ms cold. With the gateway down, the call degraded in 2.2 ms (connection refused, not the 8 s timeout path). The warm case runs two prefetch_all calls with no sync_all between them, which the real turn loop never does. The script hardcodes live-install paths.

sync_all runs after every completed turn and invalidates the scope. A FRESH hit is therefore impossible across completed turns. The only FRESH case is an interrupted turn (sync skipped) retried with the identical normalized query within 30 s. Every other repeat is served STALE, i.e. pre-write.

start_refresh uses a bare threading.Thread. The refresh therefore runs without the caller's ContextVar HERMES_HOME and secret scope, which breaks the upstream invariant. Found by code reading, not tested.

In the study-local use (exact-path local files), retrieval went from 1.54 ms cold to 0.11 ms warm and raw source reads from 3 to 1. That saves about 1.4 ms against a 1.2-2.9 s model turn, which is negligible.

features.policy_notes: It is not a new backend, so the closed-provider rule does not apply directly. But the upstream MemoryProvider.prefetch contract assigns caching to providers. byterover, honcho, openviking and retaindb implement queue_prefetch, and mem0 has a per-query cached prefetch with a hot-path wait. The motivating backend, memory_tencentdb with 3 Gateway calls per prefetch, is out of tree. The policy-aligned home is that standalone plugin, or an opt-in provider capability. A core cache that serves stale memory changes behaviour for every provider.
features.risks: Stale memory from before a write is injected unmarked for up to 300 s, which plausibly raises the stale-answer rate on exactly the supersession case z0evals#56 measures. The refresh thread may leak profile or secret scope. The real-loop hit rate is likely near zero. The branch is 6913 upstream commits behind; memory_manager hunks don't overlap, so a clean rebase is likely but unverified.

features.title: Per-provider memory prefetch outcome + latency telemetry
features.description: Emit one telemetry row per external prefetch: provider, outcome (ok, empty, timeout, inflight-skip, error), wall ms, bytes and spilled flag. Optionally add a critical-path span. Prefetch currently blocks each turn for up to 8 s per external provider with no measurement. This is the prerequisite for deciding on any cache.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/memory_manager.py::_prefetch_provider (timeout, in-flight skip, error and result branches). hermes_cli/observability/shared_metrics_loop.py (new record_provider_memory_prefetch next to record_provider_memory_call). Optionally agent/critical_path_trace.py from fork perf/critical-path-context-engine, which currently spans only context-engine select_context.

evidence.finding: Memory tool calls are instrumented. Prefetch timeouts, in-flight skips and empties are only logged at debug or warning level, with no metric.

features.policy_notes: A small core observability change in the same style as upstream's ongoing telemetry series. No provider is added.
features.risks: Telemetry volume runs at one row per turn per provider. The privacy rules for query text mean no query content may be logged.

features.title: Deterministic memory-prefetch latency/staleness probe under evals/memory/
features.description: A local fake HTTP backend with injected delay (0, 200 ms, 2 s, hang beyond 8 s), empty, error and write-then-read generations, driving the real MemoryManager through a sequence of turns with sync_all between them. It measures prefetch critical-path p50/p95, remote calls and stale-served turns, with and without the packet cache. It needs no hosted service and no inference.
features.hermes_integration_point: evals/memory/<new>.py, modelled on upstream evals/memory/honcho_current_query.py, using MemoryManager plus a fake MemoryProvider. It would replace the non-portable tools/memory_packet_runtime_check.py on the memory-packet-cache branch.

evidence.finding: Upstream already accepts deterministic memory lifecycle probes that run against a local HTTP fixture.
The prototype exists but is hardwired to <hermes-home> worktree paths and 127.0.0.1:8420. It doesn't model sync between turns.

features.policy_notes: Eval-only. It makes any memory-latency PR self-evidencing in upstream's own style.
features.risks: A fixture shows mechanism, not memory quality. Real-backend latency distributions still need E4/E5-style data.

features.title: Standalone source-backed evidence-packet plugin (pre_llm_call) with content-SHA freshness and a replay ledger
features.description: Turn the PacketBridge semantics into a standalone Hermes plugin in the z0intelligence repo: evidence refs from exact paths or AgentsView -> canonical compact packet with source_version=sha256 checked on every hit -> injected via the pre_llm_call user sidecar. Gaps and missing sources are never cached. A delivery ledger keyed on (session, turn_id, question) prevents re-injection. On any error it falls back to native Hermes behaviour.
features.hermes_integration_point: No core change. The plugin registers pre_llm_call (hermes_cli/plugins.py VALID_HOOKS) and installs into ~/.hermes/plugins or via a pip entry point. Source lives in z0intelligence harness-adapters/hermes-z0intelligence, whose stock invoke() spawns `python -m z0int.automatic` twice per turn with a 30 s timeout.

evidence.finding: The source-revision arm invalidated the cache and changed the answer. The missing-source arm abstained with a 397 B context. n=1.
Freshness keyed on content SHA catches a same-size, same-mtime replacement that z0int's mtime:size versioning misses.
The stock transport is two subprocess spawns per turn. Its overhead is unmeasured, and the lane never exercised it.

features.policy_notes: This is exactly the standalone third-party plugin path CONTRIBUTING prescribes. Nothing goes upstream.
features.risks: Subprocess cost on every turn. The process-local ledger is not durable exactly-once. The z0int automatic router path is unproven in Hermes. The plugin must keep the oracle out of the prompt.

features.title: Structured provenance channel for pre_llm_call context injection
features.description: Let pre_llm_call hooks return {context, provenance:{source ids/versions, trace_id}}, and have Hermes record the injected bytes, provenance and spill status per turn in sidecar metadata or telemetry. Today evaluators prove injection by string-matching the context in pre_api_request payloads.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/turn_context.py::_collect_pre_llm_call_context and _stamp_api_content_sidecar / _append_multimodal_context. Hook docs in hermes_cli/plugins.py.

evidence.ref: evals/unified_memory/run.py (counts of retrieval context in request_messages); tests/verify_artifacts.py
evidence.finding: Proving injection takes a custom pre_api_request capture plus substring counting. Every memory or context plugin eval must re-implement this.

features.policy_notes: A generic plugin-surface widening, which CONTRIBUTING invites in place of special-casing a plugin. It needs a maintainer to agree it is useful beyond the fork's eval needs.
features.risks: Provenance metadata could carry private locators, so it should be hashed, as the lane already does with locator_hash. It adds schema surface.

open_questions: Hermes lane vs executable-cohort.v1: should the lane switch to z0evals cohort_contract (preflight, mutation_cases, verify_answer) and its v1 answer contract, or should z0evals ship a shared consumer shim that all four harnesses import?

Does the Hermes lane need an AgentsView-backed reader, or can a preflight-approved plan be materialized into local, private exact-path snapshots without breaking the source-binding rules (retrieval-side file pins)?
Who supplies the genuine conflict_a/conflict_b contradiction pair? Until it exists, the six-case preflight stays closed for every harness.
Is memory-packet-cache deployed in the live install (<hermes-home>/hermes-agent/.worktrees/wt/memory-packet-cache)? Unverified; the live install was not inspected under the read-only rules.

Would upstream maintainers accept any core recall cache, given the MemoryProvider.prefetch contract? Or should it move into the out-of-tree memory_tencentdb plugin? This is a maintainer decision and has not been raised upstream.

If a cache is kept, should stale packets be labelled in the injected block (age, fetched before the last write) so the model can discount them? That would be measured by the stale-after-write experiment.

Do pre_llm_call hooks ever fire twice for one turn_id in real Hermes paths (preflight compression retry, detached fork)? That would justify a core-level dedupe; the lane only showed replay suppression for direct re-invocation.

summary:
All 20 issues are OPEN and were created 2026-09-30. They split into three groups.

(1) The Hermes x z0int x RLM x SoL-Pi factorial lab (#318, with S1-S5 in #319-#323). Its only running code is three stacked draft PRs (#385->#386->#387, +766 lines under lab/z0_hermes_observer): a metadata-only observer spool, a shadow question `api.attempt_will_fail`, and a Brier-score evaluator. CI is blocked: the docs file SHADOW_API_FAILURE.md:20 contains a literal `/tmp` path, and the Python test jobs are still queued. No real receipt cohort exists and no factorial cell has run.

(2) The Bend proof verifier (#324, PR #325, exp/bend-hermes-verify@55afb244, +3015 lines). This has by far the strongest evidence. I checked the CI artifacts myself:
- 225/225 matrix runs, 200/200 concurrency runs, 0/25 TOCTOU forged passes.
- Poisoning the shared kernel cache gives 10/10 (and 25/25) forged passes. With the session-pinned kernel that drops to 0/10, warm p50 is 209 ms and bootstrap is 29.5 s.
- Stock Bend 2.0.32, 2.0.33 and 2.0.34 all mis-certify bendlang#1212 (the source returns False, the certified BendTT returns True).
- The patched kvnloo/bend#2 fixes this and shows 0 mismatches over an 84-file x 2-repeat corpus (336 runs). That corpus result is not yet posted on #389.

(3) Upstream promotion queues (#313-#317). They set the existing convention: rebuild as one commit on upstream main on a `promote/<slug>-v2` branch, and promote one review slot at a time. NousResearch#129524, #129525 and #129526 are open with no reviews yet.

RFC-2 (SoL-Pi), RFC-3 (OMP) and RFC-4 (RLM) have no code in the fork. The branches lab/track1/z0int-shadow-v0, lab/track2/solpi-observation-shadow-v0 and lab/track4/rlm-state-shadow-v0, announced in comments, exist neither on the remote nor in h.git. The only Hermes R-lane code is study/hermes-unified-memory-56@c8466388. It is a local worktree, never pushed, smoke-only with n=1. Its blocker (no frozen cohort) was since cleared by z0evals#59, but the lane has not been re-run.

Architecture check against upstream main: every track can be built with zero core changes using surfaces that already exist:
- the observer hooks;
- pre_llm_call for ephemeral context;
- the llm_request / llm_execution / tool_request / tool_execution middleware;
- `register_context_engine` and `register_tool`;
- the `pre_verify` stop gate, which is the natural home for Bend W9.

Upstream policy (plugins/AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) closes in-tree third-party plugins. So Bend and z0 promote as standalone repos plus SHA-pinned plugin-catalog entries that pass `hermes plugins validate`, not as core PRs.

Closest promotable slices:
- (a) kvnloo/bend#2 to bendlang/bend: the evidence is complete.
- (b) The Bend verifier as a standalone plugin, after W6-W8.
- (c) The z0 observer as a standalone plugin, after fixing the trace-id mismatch and CI.
- (d) The adjacent core-perf branch memory-packet-cache: needs a maintainer decision.

No track has a measured Hermes task-success or token delta yet.
architecture_notes:
Checked against upstream main in wt0 (663362680b) and h.git main (298a01c79b).

**Plugin system** (hermes_cli/plugins.py)
- Discovery order is bundled plugins/<name>/, then ~/.hermes/plugins/, then ./.hermes/plugins/ (opt-in), then pip entry points.
- The lab/ directory used by #385-#387 is on no discovery path. Those plugins must be copied into ~/.hermes/plugins to load.
- PluginContext offers register_tool (L457), register_cli_command, register_context_engine (L717), register_hook (L974), register_middleware (L978) and register_system_prompt_section.
- VALID_HOOKS (L109) already includes pre/post_api_request, api_request_error, pre/post_auxiliary_call (an aux-only split, #79733), pre/post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, transform_api_error_classification, pre_llm_call, pre_verify, subagent_start/stop and on_session_*.
- Hook callbacks are bounded: 30 s timeout, then 60 s suppression (hermes_cli/plugins_dispatch.py:53,153). That makes them structurally fail-open.

**Identity**
- api_request_id = f"{turn_id}:api:{api_call_count}" (agent/conversation_loop.py:1652). It stays the same across retries within one call, so retry_count is what distinguishes physical attempts.
- Tool hooks carry task_id, session_id, tool_call_id, turn_id and api_request_id (model_tools.py:_CallIds L649).
- Upstream has no native trace_id. #385 derives trace_id = sha256(session_id + NUL + turn_id), which is turn-scoped. z0intelligence adapters/hermes_z0int/adapter.py:normalize_envelope falls back to trace_id = session_id, which is session-scoped. The same turn therefore gets different trace_ids, which violates #318's acceptance rule "exact trace identity joins all receipts". #319 had said to reuse normalize_envelope.

**Seams per track**
- Z (z0int decisions)
  - Shadow: the observer hooks (done in #385).
  - Active routing: llm_request middleware, which rewrites api_kwargs per physical call (agent/turn_api_request.py:143-153).
  - Active retry/fallback: transform_api_error_classification.
- R (RLM / State Packet)
  - Phase 2: pre_llm_call ephemeral context (agent/turn_context.py:766).
  - Phase 3, "transcript = audit log": llm_request middleware rewriting messages per request, or a ContextEngine plugin (agent/context_engine.py ABC; selected via context.engine).
- S (SoL-Pi ObservationPack)
  - Shadow: post_tool_call receives the computer_use result after serialization (a JSON string or a `_multimodal` dict), not the CaptureResult object (tools/computer_use/backend.py:63).
  - transform_tool_result is str-only ("first string return wins", model_tools.py:849-866), so it cannot carry a multimodal projection.
  - tool_execution middleware (hermes_cli/middleware.py:143) can wrap the call and return any result type, so active mode needs no core change.
- Bend
  - register_tool, plus the pre_verify hook (agent/turn_stop_gates.py:_pre_verify_nudge). That hook fires only when the turn edited files, and returns {action: continue, message} to keep the turn going. This is exactly the W9 edit-loop gate, as a pure plugin.
- Memory: MemoryManager._prefetch_provider (agent/memory_manager.py:457) has no answer cache. A hung provider costs up to _EXTERNAL_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S = 8.0 s per turn.

**Policy**
- plugins/AGENTS.md: plugins never touch core.
- "No new third-party-product plugins (June 2026)", and a hook with no concrete consumer is rejected as speculative.
- plugin-catalog/README.md: entries are human-merged, need a 40-hex SHA pin, declared capabilities must match what is registered, `hermes plugins validate` runs a security scan, and self-updaters are banned.
- The Bend plugin uses `from tools.registry import tool_error, tool_result`. Internal import paths are declared not-API, a risk for a standalone repo.
- Its process-global kernel state (_state, BoundedSemaphore(4)) needs a profile/tenant review under the multi-profile gateway (W8).

**Bend plugin specifics** (verify_core.py)
- 30 s warm budget, 120 s cold-bootstrap budget.
- Strips BENDTT, BEND_HUB, BEND_LIB and BEND_ORIGIN from the environment.
- Requires the basename PROOF.bend and the exact `ALL PROOFS CHECK` line.
- Snapshots the local import closure, then re-captures it and returns `unstable` on drift.
- Hashes the binary and kernel before and after, and reaps the process group on timeout.

**Lab branch base**: bddd22be, which is 150 commits behind upstream main and 11 behind fork main. The branches only add new files, except PR #325's three workflow files under .github/workflows, which the CI-review bot flags as sensitive.

features.title: Bend proof verifier tool (bend_verify) as an opt-in standalone Hermes plugin
features.description: A single tool, bend_verify(project_dir, proof_file='PROOF.bend'), that runs `bend PROOF.bend --verdict` without a shell. It takes an immutable local-import snapshot, strips the trust-path environment variables, and returns a typed verdict (pass / fail / indeterminate / unstable / timeout) plus a receipt: input manifest, proof, binary and kernel SHA-256 hashes, Bend version and duration. Hermes orchestrates; Bend verifies.
features.hermes_integration_point: plugins/bend/{__init__,tools,verify_core,session_kernel}.py on exp/bend-hermes-verify@55afb244, registered via PluginContext.register_tool (hermes_cli/plugins.py:457) in toolset 'bend', check_fn = shutil.which('bend'). For promotion it moves to a standalone repo plus a plugin-catalog/<name>.yaml entry with a SHA pin, validated by `hermes plugins validate`. The 3 bend-*.yml workflows must stay downstream.

evidence.finding: 225 real Bend 2.0.34 runs across 9 cases x 25 iterations, 0 mismatches. Case p50s range from 116.7 ms (missing-laws-import) to 206.6 ms (unicode path). Custom basename and symlink escape are rejected with typed error codes.

200 concurrency runs at 1/2/4/8/16 workers, 0 verdict mismatches. The LAWS-swap TOCTOU attack went from 25/25 forged passes before the snapshot fix to 0/25 after, with 25/25 source mutations detected as `unstable`.
1,897 deterministic contract cases are reported passing locally (output protocol, bounds, version parsing, env poisoning, paths). I did not re-run them in this phase.

Five adapter bugs were found and fixed downstream: ambient BENDTT/BEND_HUB/BEND_LIB/BEND_ORIGIN, arbitrary proof basenames, substring pass-marker matching, source drift between capture and verdict, and symlink escape.

features.policy_notes: In-tree plugins/bend/ conflicts with the 'No new third-party-product plugins' rule (plugins/AGENTS.md; CONTRIBUTING.md L88-101). The compliant route is a standalone repo plus a catalog entry with a 40-hex SHA pin, matching declared capabilities and a passing security scan. Subprocess use will likely draw a 'caution' finding. The RFC already anticipates this (W12 extraction).
features.risks: The plugin imports tools.registry.tool_error/tool_result, which are internal paths and not API. Kernel state is process-global (_state, semaphore of 4), and isolation across profile, gateway and subagent scopes is untested (W8). Waves W6 (failure injection), W7 (receipt replay), W11 (OS/version) and W12 are not run. The PR's full-repo CI never completed (nix flake check is queued). A stock-Bend PASS does not attest source semantics (see bend-semantic-release-qualification).

features.title: Session-pinned BendTT kernel trust root (build once per process, hash-gate every verdict)
features.description: Build a private BendTT kernel once per Hermes process under a temporary HOME, then pin its exact path and SHA-256. Every later verdict uses that pinned kernel and bypasses the mutable ~/.bend/bendtt cache, with before/after hashing of both kernel and binary. Callers fail closed with bend_integrity or kernel_integrity if either changes.
features.hermes_integration_point: plugins/bend/session_kernel.py:verify_with_session_kernel (exp/bend-hermes-verify@55afb244). Harness: evals/bend_adapter_kernel_strategies.py.

evidence.ref: Actions run 36693265577 @692128af (kvnloo#388 comment) and run 36695128005 @55afb244, artifact bend-hermes-kernel-strategies.json
evidence.finding: The baseline discriminator (bendlang/bend#1193) is verified to fail before any poisoning. Shared-cache poisoning: 10/10 forged passes. Session-pinned: 0/10 forged, 10/10 private-kernel mutations rejected, 40 runs with 0 mismatches, warm p50 208.6 ms, bootstrap 29,512.7 ms (29,176.6 ms in the earlier run).

Shared-cache poison attack: 25/25 forged passes. A fresh HOME per call has 0 mismatches but costs p50 37,425.8 ms and p95 45,234.5 ms, so session pinning is about 74x cheaper per verification at 100 calls (503.7 ms amortized).
The first W4 fixture was invalid (its baseline was already `pass`), and its 25/25 number was retracted and replaced by the #1193 oracle. This is good scientific hygiene and should stay recorded.

features.policy_notes: Same placement as the parent plugin. The pattern (pin and hash an external verifier per session) could become a reusable recipe for any verifier tool, but nothing generic is needed in core.
features.risks: The 29.5 s cold bootstrap holds a global lock on the first call. HOME is swapped for bootstrap while ELAN_HOME is preserved. Orphan-process cleanup on timeout was added (a0cdf5d3) but has not been measured under the W8 lifecycle (cancel, subagent, gateway).

area: lab-infra: experiment specification, execution, measurement and freezing (Evolution Lab, Tokenomics, Kerdoios, AODL catalog, z0evals) as they apply to Hermes
summary:
The lab already has every stage of an experiment pipeline, but the stages are split across repos, and Hermes is the least-instrumented harness in it. The stages are: spec (genomes, autoresearch config, capacity-queue items, study manifests, receipt schemas); execution (CPU sweeps, GPU-serial campaigns, paired runners, CI matrices); measurement (tokenomics.event.v0, z0int receipts, observer spools); gates (non-inferiority, paired bootstrap, Brier vs base rate); and freezing (z0evals import with a pinned SHA plus an allowlist).

The Hermes gap is concrete. ~/.z0int/tokenomics/events.jsonl holds 315 rows and none of them are harness=hermes, while OMP alone emitted 7,979 tokenomics.event.v0 rows on 2026-09-19. The Hermes emitter (tokenomics integrations/hermes.py) exists but nothing calls it. The common Hermes receipt runner in kvnloo#322 is only a 73-line schema. The observer and shadow PRs kvnloo#385–#387 have red CI.

Upstream Hermes already has the right execution template. evals/core_tool_deferral and evals/toolperf_abeval run real AIAgent cells against pinned checkouts, each in an isolated HERMES_HOME. Grading is programmatic, runs are resume-safe, cells run in parallel, and an infra-abort fuse stops broken batteries. A maintainer used this harness for the 288-run verdict on NousResearch#97979. evals/token_accounting/replay_gates.py shows a $0 pattern: the real loop runs against a scripted fake OpenAI server.

To run hundreds of Hermes experiments automatically, five pieces need joining:
(1) one experiment manifest that links an issue/RFC to arms, frozen fixture hashes, verifier, budget tier and gates.
(2) a generalized Hermes paired runner, where an arm is a checkout plus a config overlay plus a plugin set.
(3) three provider tiers: scripted replay ($0, unlimited parallel), local llama.cpp SLMs (one RTX 3080 Ti, so latency cells must run one at a time), and free quota via Kerdoios plus the capacity queue, with paid models reserved for confirmation cells.
(4) a Tokenomics observer plugin plus the observer spool, joined by the hermes_stack_experiment envelope.
(5) mandatory gates: slice informativeness, at least 5 paired samples, and non-inferiority on verified success. Results then get frozen into z0evals.

The negative results matter as much as the positive ones:
- The fly/mushroom champion is broken on real Hermes traffic: 0.143, against a majority baseline of 0.514 and ridge at 0.643.
- Linear models match the mushroom readout on the Phase 2 corpus.
- A recovery_action canary was minted on an OOD slice that a constant predictor passes.
- The autoresearch loop ran 80 sessions with 0 keeps, because its task is saturated.

So the factory's bottleneck is informative frozen batteries and trustworthy Hermes receipts, not compute. Per-turn model routing in Hermes core was closed as not-planned (NousResearch#41190, #56655). Routing and placement work therefore has to stay in plugins or standalone repos.
architecture_notes:
Hermes facts (upstream main 663362680b, checked out read-only at wt0):
- Plugin hooks are listed in hermes_cli/plugins.py:109 (VALID_HOOKS). The ones that matter here:
  - pre/post_api_request and api_request_error: one call per provider attempt. post_api_request carries usage, api_duration and first_chunk_at (TTFB).
  - pre/post_auxiliary_call: added for auxiliary traffic (NousResearch#79733).
  - pre_llm_call: its returned context is appended to the user message.
  - pre_verify: bounded by agent.max_verify_nudges.
  - Also transform_tool_result, transform_api_error_classification, subagent_start/stop, on_session_*, and the kanban_* observers.
  - Timeouts: hook callbacks time out after plugins.hook_callback_timeout (default 30s). pre_tool_call fails closed; the other bounded hooks fail open.
- website/docs/developer-guide/observer-hooks.md defines a read-only observer contract. Behavior-changing wrappers are explicitly outside it.
- There is a first-party NeMo Relay shared-metrics/ATOF path (hermes_cli/observability/relay_shared_metrics.py). toolperf_abeval reads ATOF traces for scoring.
- The usage seam is agent/turn_usage.py:record_response_usage. Tokenomics integrations/hermes.py targets this seam, so using it there would need a core patch; the observer hooks give the same data without one.
- evals/ (70 entries) is the sanctioned home for live A/B harnesses. Results are gitignored except SUMMARY/SCORECARD files. Examples: toolperf_abeval (arms differ only by PYTHONPATH), core_tool_deferral (worker.py runs in an isolated temp HERMES_HOME with a hermetic env; orchestrator.py adds --parallel, resume and an infra fuse; report.py), compaction (includes a Jev arm), token_accounting/replay_gates.py (fake OpenAI server), codebase_navigability (offline).
- batch_runner.py runs a multiprocessing Pool over JSONL prompts, with a platform=batch surface, checkpoints and tool_stats. mini_swe_runner.py and trajectory_compressor.py also exist.
- Only one ContextEngine may register.

Policy:
- Per-turn model routing plugins were closed by the sweeper as not-planned (NousResearch#41190, #56655).
- Kerdoios README: vendor/compute plugins stay standalone and are not to be PR'd into core.
- HOTL/AODL IR NousResearch#88589 is open, needs-decision.
- Harness Evolver NousResearch#110671–110676 are open at P3. kvnloo's own PR #110691 was closed by its author on 2026-09-30. Competing PR #110684 exists.
- Upstream accepts eval-backed perf/feature PRs (NousResearch#77056, #97979 by teknium1).

Fork:
- RFC-0 kvnloo#308 sets the convention: lab/<track>/<exp> branches cut from fork main bddd22be7c. Upstream receives only small evidenced PRs.
- Lab branches today: lab/z0int/{full-observer,retry-shadow,shadow-eval}-v0, lab/evals/hermes-stack-receipts-v0, lab/beyond-agent/canary-v0, exp/bend-hermes-verify.
- A promote/<slug>-v2 staging-branch convention already exists (TUI perf).

Ecosystem ownership (z0 registry docs/components; z0evals README):
- frontier-kb: evidence.
- Evolution Lab: experiment design, execution, training and qualification. Status there: branch_only / experimental.
- Tokenomics: neutral receipts. Status: merged / live, tested 9af30ca.
- z0evals: frozen studies.
- z0intelligence: promotion, shadow, canary.
- Kerdoios: placement only.
- AODL harnesses/catalog.json lists ids (hermes, omp, o8, grok, codex, claude, pi, fx) but states that a catalog row is not proof an adapter exists. The real adapters live in kvnloo/dash bridge/src/harnesses.ts (not inspected).

Hermes-facing adapters that exist:
1. Fork lab plugin z0-hermes-observer: metadata-only JSONL spool of 11 hooks, schema z0int.hermes_observer_event.v1, fails open.
2. z0intelligence adapters/hermes_z0int: normalize_envelope / close_observation / join_outcome identity.
3. z0intelligence harness-adapters/hermes-z0intelligence (branch origin/feat/claude-code-harness): an ACTIVE pre_llm_call context injector that shells out to `python -m z0int.automatic`.
4. tokenomics integrations/hermes.py (emit_provider_call): not wired.
5. Kerdoios Hermes plugin: tools kerdoios_plan/explain/inventory/record.
6. Fork exp/bend-hermes-verify: plugins/bend plus CI experiment lanes.

There is no Hermes equivalent of z0intelligence benchmarks/claude_code/run_pair.py. That runner defines arms as flag sets, interleaves and reverses arms per rep, writes create-only JSONL, records billed usage plus Tokenomics receipts, and runs a programmatic verifier.

summary:
Read-only sweep of 7 z0evals studies: slm-router-v0, z0intelligence-function-routing, unified-memory-v0, claude-code-savings-v0 (branch only, no PR), causal-ablation-v0 (PR #76), agentweb-emma-z0-v0 (PR #68), and the researching-the-frontier synthesis (PR #66). Where raw data was available locally I recomputed the numbers.

Reproduced exactly:
- Phase 1B per-arm success, Wilson CIs, warm p50 latency and residency, from openjev results/phase1b/p1b-20260921T1430Z/observations.jsonl. All 24/24 SHA256SUMS pass.
- Jev authored144: accuracy, family-balanced accuracy, AUROC and balanced accuracy match. ECE does not match exactly (I get 0.0306 vs 0.0334).
- The causal-ablation audit regenerates byte-identical (sha a63a0490...).
- Cerebras A/B totals match the receipts.
- State Packet aggregates match z0int f2ea159.

Critical corrections the z0evals publications have not absorbed:
1. Selection safety is not supported. z0intelligence 6f3345e (only on origin/feat/steal-sweep) has results/phase1b/.../analysis/claim-status.json, which marks "compiler prevents dangerous SELECTION" as INVALID. A fresh paired run had 0 dangerous selections in every cell; the 6/84 does not replicate. Only removing dangerous options from the menu holds (20/140 exposed vs 0/140).
2. The compiler-vs-unfiltered accuracy comparison is rank-deficient: both arms rendered byte-identical prompts.
3. Nemotron was silently capped at 256 tokens. At a 1024 cap it scores 0.857 (n=28, preliminary) instead of 0.619. Qwen9B needs a rerun.

slm-router-v0 still claims "compiler-restores-safety" (6/84), and causal-ablation-v0 reuses those contrasts. Both source commits are now pushed (z0int f721f8c; evolution-lab 659b5a8 is an ancestor of origin/experiment/q-route-v0 4cf52bb), so the study can be frozen, but only together with an erratum. The function-routing evidence JSONL is not in the cited commit 78869d9; it is public in z0int origin/master 28927fa.

Most Hermes-relevant evidence (Claude Code, Sonnet, small n):
- ObservationPack on long sessions: -30.3% total cost, Wilcoxon p=0.0068, 12/12 verified both arms. It stacks with lean: a further -38.2% median, p=0.031. No effect on short tasks.
- State Packet plus lean: -61% on pinned held-out tasks, 22/22 vs 21/22.
- Delegation increased parent tokens in every measured cohort.

Upstream context:
- Hermes already has the seams Claude Code lacks: the transform_tool_result hook, ContextEngine.select_context/prune_tool_results_only, register_system_prompt_section, memory providers.
- Teknium's 2026-09-19 compaction scorecard rejected tool-result removal as the primary compaction because it breaks the prompt cache. It named identifier and anchor retention as the real gap.
- So a Hermes ObservationPack must pack immediately (cache-safe) and must beat the existing 100k-char spill and proactive prune.

Not yet measured in Hermes: unified memory has 4 smoke receipts at n=1, and its frozen cohort preflight is blocked on the conflict_a/conflict_b slots. The observer/shadow lab branches have tests only, no results. Every Claude Code and State Packet runner needs paid inference. Phase 1B, token-cap, compiler-ablation, composition, the causal audit, Jev recompute and the Hermes shadow scorer can run on local models or offline.

features.title: ObservationPack (SoL-Pi) immediate tool-output packing for long sessions
features.description: Pack large tool outputs into structured, addressable observations at tool-result time, opt-in for long sessions. Measured -30.3% billed cost on a long recall task in Claude Code. In Hermes it must be cache-safe (applied before first cache write) and must beat the existing 100k-char spill and cache-aware proactive prune.
features.hermes_integration_point: Plugin on the transform_tool_result hook (hermes_cli/plugins.py VALID_HOOKS), interacting with tools/tool_result_storage.py (maybe_persist_tool_result; defaults in tools/budget_config.py: DEFAULT_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS=100_000, DEFAULT_PREVIEW_SIZE_CHARS=1_500, MCP 50_000) and agent/context_compressor.py prune_tool_results_only (cache-aware). Avoid ContextEngine.select_context deferred rewrite (breaks cache). Measure with evals/compaction/runner.py plus a cost arm.

evidence.finding: n=12 long recall: total $4.159->$2.900 (-30.3%), median paired -26.7%, 9/12 cheaper, Wilcoxon p=0.0068, 12/12 verified both arms; cache_read median 663,386 -> 134,461. Sample extended after interim looks at n=3 and n=6 (disclosed).
lean -> lean+obspack: median -38.2%, total $1.399->$0.876, 6/6 cheaper, Wilcoxon p=0.03125, 6/6 verified both arms
Short or mixed tasks are null: median -1.3% (sign p=0.219, n=6) and +0.26% (sign p=1.0, n=6). The model self-truncates, and Claude Code natively spills over ~30k chars.

Upstream rejected programmatic tool-result removal as primary compaction: it multiplies cache breaks; jev 75.5%@115K vs shipped summary+session_search 78.9%@55K. Counter-evidence for any deferred-rewrite port.

features.risks: Validated only in Claude Code on a deliberately output-heavy task. Hermes proactive prune may already capture most of the gain. Packing before the model sees the output can hide needed bytes. The n=12 and s2 rows were hand-transcribed into summary.json: summarize.py does not compute Wilcoxon, and the raw run JSONL is on another host (mbp), not found here.
features.policy_notes: Upstream measures recall vs retained tokens vs cache breaks (evals/compaction). A PR must show cost and recall noninferiority against current+session_search recovery, and must be immediate (cache-neutral).

features.title: z0 State Packet: provenance-pointed current-state injection at session start with explicit abstention
features.description: Compile 'what is true now' from git, docs and session history, with a source pointer on every claim, and inject it at session start as an aid to tools, not a replacement. The abstention rule must distinguish 'source unavailable' from 'nothing recorded'.
features.hermes_integration_point: register_system_prompt_section(position='after_memory') or register_memory_provider (plugins/memory/*), plus the on_session_start / pre_llm_call hooks. Fork MemoryPacketCache: agent/memory_packet_cache.py + agent/memory_manager.py on fork/memory-packet-cache@3e762e9d8f. Eval lane: evals/unified_memory/* on study/hermes-unified-memory-56@c84663880a.

evidence.finding: Pinned held-out, 22 trials/cell. stock+raw 21/22 $2.186; stock+packet 22/22 $1.815 (factor 0.83); lean+raw 20/22 $1.063; lean+packet 22/22 $0.861 (-61%). Predicted 0.404 vs observed 0.394. Tool calls 5.55 -> 3.23 mean.

Held-out: packet+tools 14/14 vs raw tools 12/14, half the tool calls, -30% mean / -53% median input tokens. Packet-only 8/14; injected abstention 0/4, fixed to 4/4 on the dev set (results_postfix.json, written after seeing the failure).
Hermes live smoke, n=1 per arm, not a frozen cohort. cold 2910 ms (retrieval 1.54 ms) vs warm 1234 ms (0.11 ms); context 1061 bytes; abstention verified; replay suppressed with model_called=false.

features.risks: Measured on Claude Code current-work questions, not on Hermes tasks. Answer keys drift: two went stale overnight. Overlaps upstream's many memory providers (honcho, mem0, holographic, ...).
features.policy_notes: Upstream does not want a new memory database (the study rules say so too). Ship as a memory-provider or system-prompt-section plugin; measure against session_search recovery.

features.title: Exact-identifier and anchor retention across compaction and memory
features.description: Retain delegation ids, root causes, config keys and exact error strings verbatim, with provenance, through summarization. Upstream itself named this as the summary's failure mode, and it is the 'exact-identifier' question in the unified-memory cohort.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/context_compressor_summary.py / conversation_compression*.py summary prompt plus an anchor index. Eval: evals/compaction/runner.py recall exam, plus the unified-memory exact-identifier / missing-evidence questions (z0evals executable-cohort.v1.json).

evidence.finding: 'the facts our summary loses (delegation ids, root causes, config keys, exact error strings) sat in assistant text. That is a summariser-retention target (anchor index / identifier capture)'
Frozen exact-identifier/missing-evidence prompts (prompt ids f568cad4...) with a literal-span oracle. Not yet run: READINESS.json preflight.passed=false.

features.risks: The recall exam has ~±3.3 pt noise at 15 questions. Needs an auxiliary LLM judge (paid Nous route upstream).
features.policy_notes: Directly answers a gap upstream itself named. Smallest footprint, highest fit.

features.title: Lean per-session prefix and task-conditioned skill exposure
features.description: Cut the static per-session prefix (skill listings, MCP, user hooks) that is rewritten on every cold session and re-read on every request. Hide irrelevant skills only if a selector can meet the 'hide a needed skill at most once in 30' bar.
features.hermes_integration_point: Skill index rendering into the system prompt (prompt builder / skills toolset), core tool deferral (evals/core_tool_deferral, evals/tool_search), evals/prompt_footprint, evals/token_accounting/worktree_prompt_prefix.py.

evidence.finding: Cold sessions: median -64.7%, 10/10 cheaper, sign p=0.002, quality 10/10 in both arms
Warm: 20 pairs, median -29.5%, 20/20 cheaper, sign p=2e-6. README warm-only: -27.2% median, 15/15. Cold start costs ~3x warm ($0.126 vs $0.0425).
Hiding 45 skills saves ~5.7k prefix tokens, but the lexical selector had 3/30 misses and decider-2b at best 2/30, so it was NOT promoted.

features.risks: Claude Code prefix structure differs from Hermes. Hiding a needed skill is a quality regression.
features.policy_notes: Upstream already measures prompt footprint and tool deferral, so this extends existing work.

features.title: Typed/compressed delegate_task results and PARENT_ONLY as a first-class outcome
features.description: Every measured cohort shows delegation increases parent work, because the parent reads the task plus a verbose worker reply. The next experiment: typed, bounded worker artifacts that replace parent work, and no automatic generic-worker offload.
features.hermes_integration_point: tools/delegate_tool.py, tools/delegate_tool_results.py (_spill_summary_to_file), agent/delegation_context.py, subagent_start/subagent_stop hooks, evals/delegation_group_schema and evals/subagent_process_handoff.

evidence.finding: Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b, reasoning none, 60 pairs (2 tasks x 30). Uncached parent input+output A 358,575 vs B 427,139 (+68,564). Equal-cache subsets: +522.1 [506.0,536.4] (12 pairs) and +1008.1 [959.1,1063.6] (8 pairs). Caveat: full-cohort per-task bootstrap CIs include zero (summary +983.5 [-2563,+4500]; gate +1302 [-2496,+4984]). Worker 60/60 raw pass.
+501 / +38 uncached parent input, +15.73 s / +24.17 s wall, repair or fallback required
A tiny-task offload added 1347 uncached parent tokens

features.policy_notes: Negative evidence does not justify upstream auto-offload. The typed-artifact hypothesis is unmeasured.

features.title: Metadata-only Hermes observer + outcome-grounded DecisionBackend shadow (Brier vs base rate)

The first shadow question, 'will this provider attempt fail?', is labeled only by Hermes lifecycle facts (post_api_request vs api_request_error). features.hermes_integration_point: lab/z0_hermes_observer plugin. Hooks: on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre/post_api_request, api_request_error, pre/post_auxiliary_call, pre/post_tool_call, subagent_stop, on_session_end. Later: decision provider API (upstream PR NousResearch#113020, open).

evidence.finding: Privacy, fail-open, join and Brier semantics are unit-tested. No measured cohort or results exist.

features.policy_notes: Labels come from lifecycle facts, never self-labeling. Emits promotion_ready=false by design.

features.title: Record effective (wire) max_tokens and classify reasoning truncation separately from refusal/empty
features.description: Phase 1B receipts recorded max_tokens=1024 while the wire sent 256 (dialect clamp). Reasoning models then returned finish_reason=length with empty content and the gold answer inside reasoning_content. Hermes should record requested vs effective caps and treat length+empty+reasoning as truncation.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/empty_response_guard.py, agent/auxiliary_reasoning_floor.py, agent/auxiliary_client.py (aux lanes with small max_tokens, e.g. title max_tokens=64), evals/token_accounting.

evidence.finding: Nemotron 57.1% -> 82.1% -> 85.7% at caps 256/512/1024; truncated 42.9% -> 0%; gold-in-reasoning 100% at every cap. Qwen3.5-4B 71.4% -> 89.3% at 256 -> 1024. Hammer/FunctionGemma cap-invariant. Schedule incomplete: 983/1176 measured, 6/14 cells complete.
4 of 6 generative arms ran under a smaller cap than their receipts recorded
Upstream already removed user output caps. Aux task budgets remain.

features.risks: The measured case was local llama.cpp dialects, not Hermes. It is unverified whether Hermes aux paths hit this.
features.policy_notes: Aligned with upstream's output-cap removal. Likely a small test-backed fix if a Hermes aux path is shown to truncate.

Framing x filter 2x2 rank-deficient (A==C, B==D byte-identical). Filter effect -7/140 (filtering cost accuracy, via truncation).

architecture_notes:
z0evals is a frozen evidence and publication layer. It owns no runtime policy, and every claim must resolve to pinned artifacts. Channels: preview carries function-routing; main carries the unified-memory scaffold (acb95ab) but not the executable cohort (667223e is a branch); claude-code-savings, causal-ablation and agentweb are branch or PR only.

Hermes seams relevant to these studies (upstream wt0 663362680b):
- Hooks (hermes_cli/plugins.py VALID_HOOKS): transform_tool_result, transform_terminal_output, pre_llm_call, pre/post_api_request, api_request_error, pre/post_auxiliary_call, on_session_start/end, subagent_start/stop, pre_verify.
- Middleware kinds: tool request, tool execution, LLM request, LLM execution.
- register_system_prompt_section (position after_memory), register_memory_provider (plugins/memory: honcho, mem0, holographic, byterover, openviking, retaindb), register_context_engine, register_auxiliary_task.
- ContextEngine (agent/context_engine.py) exposes select_context (request-only replacement, runs every request, breaks its own cache prefix), prune_tool_results_only (deterministic, cache-aware; needs min reclaim plus a regrowth runway), and on_turn_complete. These give Hermes a history-projection seam Claude Code lacks, but upstream treats cache breaks as the main cost.
- Tool output: tools/tool_result_storage.py persists large outputs to $HERMES_HOME/cache/spillover with preview plus path.
- No decision-provider registry on main; PR NousResearch#113020 is open.
- Upstream already removed user output caps (evals/output_caps_scope.md) and has empty_response_guard plus auxiliary_reasoning_floor.

Upstream eval conventions: living harnesses under evals/ (compaction recall exam with policy arms, SCORECARD files, matched-budget controls, stated noise floor ~±3.3 pt at 15 questions).

Downstream substrate:
- z0int adapters/hermes_z0int (trace normalization).
- Fork lab plugin lab/z0_hermes_observer (shadow-eval-v0).
- MemoryPacketCache (fork/memory-packet-cache 3e762e9d8f).

summary:
What exists in the KB. frontier-kb (main 22b4c0f, 2026-09-19) has 14 harness notes, 65 permanent notes, 59 literature notes and 4 Hermes plan notes. The local Postgres store `frontier_kb` is a stale snapshot: 66 real notes plus 101 smoke rows, last write 2026-09-10, no eval data. Treat the git vault as the source of truth. The Hermes items with real evidence are: harness-evolver credit gates (GSME +9.3pp, Evo-Bench +9.7), edit-tool shape (bash vs str_replace swings Qwen3.6-27B by about 20 points), SoL-Pi ObservationPack / Action Fusion, the secret portal, and the landing-evidence verifier.

Gap claims checked against Hermes main:
- **Several KB gaps are stale.** These have landed: `select_context` (dec464c351, 2026-06-23), `ContextEngine.on_turn_complete`, request middleware (`hermes_cli/middleware.py`), opt-in subagent worktree isolation (6ee58f4088), typed `delegate_task` output_schema (d6ee58b583), a verify-before-finish ledger with a `pre_verify` hook, tool_search plus core-tool deferral (#97979), and detection of stateless MCP 2026-07-28 servers.
- **Gaps that still hold:** no DAP; vault kinds are only login/payment/address; screenshots during vault fill are not frozen; the skill ledger is "TELEMETRY, NOT A GATE"; background-review `add` writes go in unverified (only replace/remove are staged for approval, #105921); there is no evolver; there is no evals/edittool on main.

Upstream has moved past the KB:
- teknium1 cited SoL-Pi ObservationPack as design evidence on PR #107731 (wire-only stale-tool-result projection). His conditions: trigger at a fixed boundary, gate on cache economics, and measure the cache-read ratio before and after.
- teknium1's Jev scorecard (2026-09-19) rejects prune-first compaction because it multiplies prompt-cache breaks. It points at identifier retention in the summary instead.
- KeyArgo ran the edittool meter (PR #111127): hermes `patch` 5/6 vs str_replace 6/6. A wrong single-line anchor applies silently through the `context_aware` fuzzy strategy (similarity 0.923).
- kvnloo closed his own evolver Phase-0 PR #110691 on 2026-09-30. The competing PR #110684 is open with 0 reviews.
- Xipong pushed back hard on making self-tuning a user-facing feature (#111237).

What is ready for promotion:
1. Edit-tool fail-loud plus the meter. Deterministic, measured, small. `fuzzy_match.py` is the one shared choke point.
2. Boundary-stable tool-result projection. Salvage #107731 using teknium's requirements, with sol-pi-hermes as the shadow donor.
3. Evolver Phase 0, reframed as offline eval tooling. Needs a completeness denominator, plausibly-bad negatives, and a noise-floor study.
4. A new suggestion: feed the evolver's trace slot from Hermes-native failure taxonomies (verification_evidence, tool_guardrails block reasons, FailoverReason, turn_exit_reason) rather than only factory JSON.

Policy constraints. Third-party integrations (Jev, SoL-Pi, memory backends, secret brokers) must ship as standalone plugins. A new core capability has to come as a widening of the generic hook or `ctx` surface, and a hook is only added together with a real call site. Every caching-adjacent change needs a measured cache-read ratio. Upstream evals report verdicts in `SUMMARY.md` files from two-arm A/B runs. The fork's RFC-2 premise that ObservationPack gives "richer structured observations" for computer use contradicts the SoL-Pi source: it projects pure-text results over 10 KiB and skips images.
architecture_notes:
Hermes extension points (verified at 663362680b):
- **Plugin hooks:** `VALID_HOOKS` at `hermes_cli/plugins.py:109` (about 50 hooks). There is no generic turn-settled hook and no plan-step hook. The code comment says hooks are added only together with real call sites.
- **Middleware:** `hermes_cli/middleware.py` defines tool_request, tool_execution, llm_request and llm_execution. llm_request runs in `agent/turn_api_request.py:143`.
- **ctx registration:** `ctx.register_middleware`, `register_tool`, `register_context_engine` and others (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:457-1159`).
- **ContextEngine** (`agent/context_engine.py`): only one is active (`context.engine`). User engines in `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/<name>` may subclass `ContextCompressor` (`agent/context_compressor.py:1974`) and so keep compression. `select_context` is request-only, runs before the cache plan and sanitizers, and fails open (`agent/conversation_loop.py:1285`). `on_turn_complete` is engine-only and best-effort (`conversation_loop.py:1342`). `prune_tool_results_only` does deterministic dedup, summarize, truncate and retire-images passes.
- **Spillover:** large tool outputs persist to `$HERMES_HOME/cache/spillover` with a 24h prune (`tools/tool_result_storage.py:45`). This makes path-based recall and sticky stubs time-bounded.
- **Request pipeline:** `assemble_api_request` (`agent/turn_request_assembly.py:106`) runs before `build_prompt_cache_plan` (`agent/prompt_caching.py:260`).
- **Edit tool:** `patch` (`tools/file_tools.py:1187`) offers old_string/new_string through `fuzzy_find_and_replace` (`tools/fuzzy_match.py:338`). It tries 9 strategies; `context_aware` is the last resort and a similarity strategy (line 261, line 302). It is shared by `file_operations.patch_replace` and `patch_parser`. `write_file` auto-lints and refuses stale writes.
- **Verification:** `agent/verification_evidence.py` is a passive ledger (`record_terminal_result` at line 456, `record_verify_run` at line 466). `agent/verification_stop.py` adds a bounded nudge, and the `pre_verify` hook is capped by `agent.max_verify_nudges`.
- **Learning loop:**
  - `agent/background_review.py` forks the agent and writes directly to the memory and skill stores.
  - `tools/memory_tool.py:166` stages replace/remove from unattended review into `tools/write_approval.py` (#105921). `add` is ungated.
  - `tools/skill_ledger.py` is an audit plus rollback with no gate.
  - `agent/curator.py` moves skills active → stale → archived based on usage timestamps.
  - Memory limits are 2200 and 1375 chars (`tools/memory_tool_store.py:99`).
  - `MemoryProvider.on_session_end` extracts with no verification.
- **Delegation:** roles are leaf or orchestrator only, with no explore/scout preset. `output_schema` gets one bounded retry (`tools/delegation_output_schema.py`). Worktree isolation is opt-in, git-only and limited to the local backend (`tools/subagent_worktree.py`).
- **Native failure taxonomies** a pathology archive can consume:
  - `tool_guardrails` decisions, e.g. `repeated_exact_failure_block` and `idempotent_no_progress_block` (`agent/tool_guardrails.py:369`).
  - The `FailoverReason` enum (`agent/error_classifier.py:34`).
  - `turn_exit_reason` strings (`agent/turn_loop_errors.py`, `turn_preflight.py`).
  - The verification ledger.
- **Eval culture:** `evals/` holds offline two-arm A/B harnesses (toolperf_abeval, readtool, compaction, core_tool_deferral, codebase_navigability). `results/` is gitignored except `SUMMARY.md`, and the verdicts are the artifact. teknium's bar for caching-adjacent changes is a cache-read ratio measured before and after.
- **CONTRIBUTING:** new memory providers and any third-party product integration must be standalone plugins. A missing capability means a request to widen the generic plugin surface.

frontier-kb invariants: it is research memory only, not personal memory. Postgres uses CAS `notes.version` and append-only events. The KB already holds the 5-slot evolver adapter (surface, open battery, sealed battery, trace stream, rollout gate) and the three gates (validity, activation, paired 2σ credit).

features.title: Wire-only tool-result projection triggered at a stable boundary and gated on cache economics (ObservationPack done the way Hermes needs)
features.description: Replace old, large, persisted tool results with stable handles in the per-request copy only; the transcript is untouched. Full body is sent twice before projecting, with a 2048 B head and 1536 B tail. Projection fires once per row at a fixed boundary (rows already behind the compaction or prune cursor, or a batch cut), never per turn by row age. A cacheWriteReadRatio-style break-even gates it. Stickiness is persisted per session, not in memory. Each stub is verified once per key. Recall is a safety valve, not the value case: Fan et al. arXiv:2609.20804, as cited by teknium, found recovery machinery rarely used.

area: arch-core: Hermes Agent core architecture (upstream main 663362680b, 2026-09-30) — turn pipeline, invariants, extension points, policies
summary:
I read upstream main at 663362680b (wt0): the root AGENTS.md and 11 area AGENTS.md files, plus the code behind them. Hermes is a narrow-waist core with a very wide edge. A turn is `AIAgent.run_conversation`. It takes a turn lease (`agent/turn_facade_lease.py`) and then calls `agent/conversation_loop.py::_run_conversation_turn`, which runs: `build_turn_context` (memory prefetch plus `pre_llm_call` context, both put on the user-message `api_content` sidecar) → a while-loop of phase helpers, each dispatched through ONE function, `_run_phase` (begin_iteration, prepare_iteration, assemble_api_request, run_preflight_gate, the API retry loop, normalize_model_response, then run_tool_round or finish_text_response with its stop gates) → `finalize_turn` (persist, `transform_llm_output`/`post_llm_call`, `ContextEngine.on_turn_complete`, memory `sync_all` plus queued prefetch, the background-review fork, and the per-turn plugin `on_session_end`).

The invariants are:
- The system prompt is byte-stable, built in three tiers (stable / context / volatile) in `agent/system_prompt.py`.
- Compression is the only sanctioned cache break.
- Roles strictly alternate. The only synthetic user rows are `/steer` and the stop-gate nudges, appended after an assistant row.
- Profile scope is bound per activity, never read from `os.environ`.

The extension surface is already large: 41 `VALID_HOOKS`, 4 middleware kinds, 37 `PluginContext` members plus 8 scoped provider registrars, and ABCs for memory providers (one external at a time, in-tree set closed), context engines (`select_context` / `on_turn_complete`, with no bundled consumer), model providers, cron providers, platforms and approval transports. Tool-search deferral and an offline eval culture are both strong: 288-run A/B batteries, compaction recall scorecards, and fake-provider replay harnesses.

The architecture clearly invites these gaps, each backed by open upstream issues and competing PRs:
1. A unified bounded `before_turn_end` gate generalizing `pre_verify` (#101910 and 4+ PRs).
2. Compaction lifecycle hooks (#118382, #119317, #125384).
3. A turn-phase observer hook (#125255). The fork already has the code on `perf/critical-path-*`, and `_run_phase` is the natural single wrap point.
4. A summarizer identifier-retention audit of the anchor index. The 2026-09-19 scorecard names it as the remaining gap.
5. A skills-efficacy paired-arm eval (RFC #96704, PR #122544).
6. Eval-safe memory isolation (#121935).
7. Model routing restricted to cache-safe seams (auxiliary, delegation, session start).
8. Shared offline replay and promotion-gate infrastructure (fork evolver gates) as the experiment factory.

On policy: third-party products go in standalone plugin repos, never `plugins/`. That covers z0 observer, Bend, TypeSafe/Jev skill routing and memory backends. Non-secret behaviour config goes in `config.yaml`, not new `HERMES_*` env vars. Each fix ships with 1–2 invariant tests that are red on base, and anything touching resolution chains or profile scope needs E2E runs against a real temp `HERMES_HOME` (A→B→A under multiplex).
architecture_notes:
TURN PIPELINE (663362680b):
1. `run_agent.py` AIAgent facade (mixins) → `agent/turn_facade.py` takes the durable turn lease (`turn_facade_lease.py`) and binds subagent parent, interrupt scope and relay metrics.
2. `agent/conversation_loop.py::run_conversation` → `_run_conversation_turn`.
3. `agent/turn_context.py::build_turn_context` does turn setup in this order:
   - recover a rotated compression session; bind session/log ids; refresh MCP tools between turns;
   - `_restore_or_build_system_prompt` (cached `_cached_system_prompt`; the DB row is created only after the prompt exists, #45499);
   - turn-start compaction;
   - `_tick_memory_nudge`;
   - `_collect_pre_llm_call_context`: `pre_llm_call` plugins; oversized output is spilled by `tools/hook_output_spill.py` (default 10k chars);
   - `_memory_turn_start_and_prefetch`: `MemoryManager.on_turn_start` + `prefetch_all`, skipped for trivial prompts via `TRIVIAL_PROMPT_RE`;
   - context goes into the CURRENT user message's API copy, stamped as the `api_content` sidecar so replay is byte-identical.
4. `_LoopState` dataclass + `_run_phase(fn, agent, state)`: signature-inspected kwargs in, verdict fields copied back. Every phase goes through this one function. Order: begin_iteration → prepare_iteration → assemble_api_request → run_preflight_gate → announce_api_call → `_run_api_retry_loop` (nous_rate_limit_guard, build_api_request [`pre_api_request` hook + `llm_request` middleware], perform_api_call [`llm_execution` middleware], check_api_response, handle_api_interrupt / handle_api_error [`transform_api_error_classification`]) → apply_retry_restarts → normalize_model_response → `run_tool_round` (`agent/tool_executor.py`: concurrent ≤8 workers, 420s default timeout, or sequential/segmented; `INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` table for agent-level tools; `tool_request`/`tool_execution` middleware; pre/post_tool_call; tool_search bridge unwrap) OR `finish_text_response` → `turn_stop_gates.apply_stop_gates` (verify-on-stop evidence nudge → `pre_verify` hook, only after code edits → kanban terminal-call guard).
5. `turn_finalizer.finalize_turn`, in order: persist (micro-compaction is opt-in) → file-mutation footer → `transform_llm_output` + `post_llm_call` → `ContextEngine.on_turn_complete` → surrogate scrub → `_sync_external_memory_for_turn` (`sync_all` + `queue_prefetch`) → `_spawn_background_review` (forked AIAgent on the same cached prefix, tool whitelist, writes memory/skills) → plugin `on_session_end`, which fires EVERY turn despite its name. Real boundaries use `on_session_finalize` / provider `on_session_end`.
6. `run_conversation` exports the turn boundary, and `_close_durable_failed_turn` appends a Hermes-authored assistant row so the durable tail never ends on a user row.

INVARIANTS:
- **Prompt cache:**
  - The system prompt is byte-stable for the conversation; compression is the only sanctioned break, and `invalidate_system_prompt` reloads memory and re-renders plugin sections only then.
  - Tiers are stable (identity, guidance, pinned skills, coding brief) → context (`system_message`, AGENTS.md/context files, workspace) → volatile (skills index, memory, plugin sections `after_memory` only, profile line, timestamp, runtime env).
  - Mid-conversation injection rides a user message or tool result: skills slash commands, `subdirectory_hints` (32k cap), `pre_llm_call`, gateway notes.
  - Slash commands that mutate prompt state default to deferred invalidation with an opt-in `--now`.
- **Roles:** strict alternation and no synthetic mid-loop user message. The exceptions are `/steer` (a user row after the tool row) and stop-gate nudges (user rows after an assistant answer, flagged `_*_synthetic`). Async delegation and background-process completions arrive as NEW turns via `process_registry.completion_queue`; cron runs in its own session.
- **Profile scope:** one process serves many profiles. Code outside a turn binds scope explicitly (`_profile_runtime_scope`, `@_profile_scoped`, `_profile_cron_scope`, `_run_release_in_profile_scope`). Secrets go through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`; threads through `spawn_context_thread`; child env through `build_subprocess_env` / `served_profile_child_env`; `check_fn` cache is keyed by `hermes_home_key()`.
- **Code shape:**
  - facade + `<stem>_<topic>` siblings; split at ~2,000-line files or ~300-line / CC-30 functions;
  - no ≥4-branch `elif` ladders on names (tables instead);
  - no re-export shims;
  - no defensive `try/except: pass`;
  - never hardcode `~/.hermes`;
  - never infer process identity from argv substrings.

FOOTPRINT LADDER: extend existing → CLI command + skill → service-gated tool (`check_fn`: reachability/opt-in only, never session surface) → plugin (`~/.hermes/plugins` or pip entry point) → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (last resort; every schema ships on every call). Session-dependent surfaces are named toolsets folded in by `_load_enabled_toolsets(platform)`. Tool-search (`tools/tool_search.py`) defers MCP, plugin and curated core tools behind `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call`; `clarify` is deliberately never deferred (A/B 18/18 → 7/18).

EXTENSION POINTS:
- **`VALID_HOOKS` (41):**
  - Turn: pre/post_tool_call, transform_terminal_output, transform_tool_result, transform_llm_output, pre/post_llm_call, on_stream_start/delta/end, on_interim_message, pre_verify, pre/post_api_request, api_request_error, pre/post_auxiliary_call, transform_api_error_classification.
  - Session: on_session_start/end/finalize/reset, on_skill_lifecycle, subagent_start/stop.
  - Gateway: pre_gateway_dispatch, agent_loop_stopped, pre/post_approval_request/response, on_room_member_activity, pre_transcription, gateway_platform_event, pre_command.
  - Kanban: 3 task hooks + 5 on_kanban_* hooks.
- **Hook behaviour:** default timeout 30s, max 600s; `pre_tool_call` fails closed on timeout.
- **Middleware:** `tool_request`, `tool_execution`, `llm_request`, `llm_execution` (`hermes_cli/middleware.py`).
- **PluginContext:** register_tool (override needs the `tools.override` capability), register_hook/middleware, register_system_prompt_section (≤4k each / 8k total, frozen per session), register_skill (namespaced, not in the index), register_command / register_cli_command, register_context_engine (single), register_context_reference (`@prefix:`), register_auxiliary_task (own `auxiliary.<key>` config), register_platform / platform handlers, register_approval_transport, register_redaction_patterns, register_locale*, emit/subscribe event bus, ctx.llm (host-owned completions), ctx.subagent_lifecycle (launch/status/wait/cancel/result/reconnect handles), call_mcp (per-server allowlist), inject_message (gateway needs `allow_gateway_injection`), dispatch_tool, spawn_task, on_unload. Scoped registrars cover image_gen, video_gen, web_search, browser, terminal_environment, secret_source, tts, transcription.
- **ABCs:**
  - `MemoryProvider`: builtin + ONE external; is_available, initialize(agent_context primary|subagent|cron|flush), system_prompt_block (static), prefetch / queue_prefetch, sync_turn, on_pre_compress (checkpoint API v2), on_session_switch/end, on_delegation, on_memory_write, tools via `check_fn`.
  - `ContextEngine`: should_compress/compress, prune_tool_results_only, request-only `select_context`, `on_turn_complete`, `clone_for_agent`.
  - Others: ProviderProfile (model-providers, last-writer-wins), cron providers, dashboard auth, `SecretSource`.
- **Other surfaces:** shell hooks (`hooks:` config, consented, exit 2 blocks), outbound webhooks (`hooks.outbound`, HMAC), skill bundles, skills `auto_load`, cron `script` / `context_from` / `no_agent`, kanban toolset (zero footprint outside tasks), /goal, /loop, /review, /btw, /moa, /learn, /plan, batch_runner + toolset_distributions, `mini_swe_runner`, `trajectory_compressor`.

POLICIES:
- `plugins/memory/` is closed to new providers (honcho, mem0, supermemory, byterover, holographic, openviking, retaindb stay; hindsight moved to the catalog). New backends are standalone repos on the same ABC.
- No new third-party-product plugins in tree (observability, SaaS, analytics, paid tie-ins); they ship as standalone repos and enter the catalog with a SHA-pinned `plugin-catalog/*.yaml`.
- Plugins never touch core: widen the generic surface instead. A hook with no concrete consumer is speculative and rejected. When 3+ PRs integrate one category, design the ABC/hook first.
- Compat is a behavior contract: additive kwargs, signature-inspected callbacks.
- `.env` holds secrets only.
- No change-detector tests, no tests that read source, no faked host OS.
- Use `scripts/run_tests.sh` only (CI parity, per-file subprocess isolation).
- 1–2 invariant tests red on base per fix.
- E2E against a real temp `HERMES_HOME` for resolution chains, config, security and profile scope (A→B→A multiplex).
- Every `DEFAULT_CONFIG` key needs a reader plus an invariant test through the consuming loader.

features.title: Unified bounded before_turn_end continuation gate (generalize pre_verify)
features.description: One directive hook at the final-response chokepoint that fires for every non-interrupted text completion, not just after code edits. It returns allow / continue(message, hide draft) / fail(safe message) under a Hermes-owned budget, so retrieval-enforcing memory providers, policy gates and claim-evidence checks can rework an answer before it streams, persists or delivers. It reuses the existing stop-gate `_continue` pattern: a synthetic user nudge row after the assistant row keeps role alternation legal. The claim gate (#124747) and the passive `agent/verification_evidence.py` ledger become plugin consumers.
features.hermes_integration_point: agent/turn_stop_gates.py::apply_stop_gates (add a 4th gate; reuse _continue/_append_interim_answer); agent/turn_final_response.py; agent/turn_finalizer.py (withhold stream/TTS while under review); hermes_cli/plugins.py VALID_HOOKS + plugins_dispatch.py directive parser (model on get_pre_verify_continue_message); agent/shell_hooks.py _RESPONSE_PARSERS; config agent.max_final_continuations (bounded like agent.max_verify_nudges)

evidence.finding: memleaf-style providers need current-turn search before an answer escapes; transform_llm_output cannot continue the loop, pre_verify is coding-only, sync_turn is post-hoc
pre_verify fires only when `_edited and has_hook('pre_verify')`; stop gates already append flagged synthetic user rows after the assistant answer

evidence.ref: Competing open PRs NousResearch#124956 (+836), #128724 (+814), #68142 (+56), #124747 claim gate (+188)
